body:
Title: introduce-capacity-circuit-breaker-and-windowed-cooldown-for-dedicated-fleets

Description: This PR adds a capacity-level circuit breaker and a windowed cooldown policy to the Dedicated autoscaler. Motivation: during multi-tenant surges we've observed cascading scale-ups that drive temporary but significant cost and destabilize downstream provisioners. The circuit breaker prevents aggressive immediate scale-outs by limiting new allocation commits for a configurable short window when utilization growth exceeds a confidence threshold. The windowed cooldown provides a sliding observation window to progressively re-enable allocations as utilization stabilizes instead of a fixed cooldown timer.

Design summary: Implemented a light-weight circuit_breaker component used by the reservation allocator. The breaker tracks recent allocation decisions and a statistically smoothed utilization delta computed by the new windowed_cooldown component. It exposes a decision API Evaluate(requestContext) => {allow|throttle|fast_fail, reason}. Key behaviors: (1) short-circuit fast-fail for large concurrency spikes when downstream provisioning shows >90th percentile latency degradation; (2) throttle (soft deny) mode which returns allow=false but records a deferred request for backoff; (3) progressive re-open using an exponential-convergence window where allowance increases as rolling-utilization shows nominal behavior.

Telemetry and observability: added metrics for circuit_breaker_evaluations_total{decision}, circuit_breaker_open_duration_seconds, windowed_util_delta_percentile, and per-tenant throttled_allocations. Added metric registration and dashboards (docs/observability/capacity-circuit-breaker.md) with recommended alert rules for persistent open state.

Compatibility and defaults: Feature is off by default for all fleets. A Helm value redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.circuitBreaker.enabled=false controls rollout. The canary manifest deploys the component to a single small Dedicated pool for live experiments. Default thresholds are conservative (scale-out throttle at 25% sustained delta in the 60s window, open if combined with provisioning latencies above 95th pct).

Testing and CI: Unit tests for windowing math and breaker state transitions; integration test simulating step load with a fake provisioner. CI: initial run failed on lint (golangci-lint) which was fixed in a follow-up commit. Integration suite passed on rerun. Canary rollout was exercised in staging for 48 hours before merge.

Commits: init: add capacity circuit breaker core and windowing primitives; feat(autoscaler): integrate circuit breaker with reservation reconciler; chore(test): add integration tests; fix(lint): address go vet; docs: observability guide.

Files changed (high level):
- services/autoscaler/circuit_breaker.go: new state machine, evaluation API, unit tests in same package.
- services/autoscaler/windowed_cooldown.go: sliding-window util delta estimator (reservoir + EWMA hybrid).
- pkg/api/v1alpha/autoscaler.proto: added CRD fields for enabling circuit breaker and tuning knobs.
- cmd/observe/metrics/registration.go: register new metrics and export to prometheus client.
- helm/charts/redwood-dedicated/values.yaml: feature toggle and sane defaults.
- infra/k8s/manifests/dedicated-autoscaler-canary.yaml: canary deployment manifest and RBAC.
- docs/observability/capacity-circuit-breaker.md: operational guidance and dashboard links.
- tests/integration/test_circuit_breaker.py: integration flow that asserts stability under burst and slow-provision scenarios.
- README.md: short note on configuration and rollout plan.

Review conversation (high level):
- Evan: "We need clearer invariants around when the breaker moves to 'open' vs 'throttle'. Please add unit tests for corner cases and document the math."
- Maya(reply): "Added unit tests for the corner cases (zero baseline, negative deltas) and expanded comments in windowed_cooldown.go to spell out the math and invariants."
- Priya: "Telemetry looks good, but tie the open-duration metric to an alerting suggestion in docs."
- Maya: "Added recommended PromQL in docs and example alert rules; moved metric to top-level registry to avoid double-registration in short-lived test harnesses."
- Liam: "Suggest default thresholds be conservative; prefer feature off-by-default for existing customers."
- Maya: "Default set to off; documented canary and rollout steps."

CI summary: initial CI (lint) failed due to exported var name and a minor formatting issue. Fix applied and CI was re-run. Full test matrix passed (unit, integration, e2e canary smoke). PR merged via squash on 2026-03-04 after approving reviewers and green CI.

Merge outcome and rollout: Squash merge into main. Feature flag gated; chart values added so SRE can flip on per-fleet. Staging canary observed ~35% reduction in emergency scale-outs for a simulated noisy tenant with negligible impact to successful request admission. Next steps: gather two weeks of telemetry, tune heuristics, and expose a per-tenant override API for platform teams.
release_notes: Add capacity circuit breaker and windowed cooldown policy for Dedicated autoscaler. Feature off by default; can be enabled per-fleet via Helm. Adds telemetry metrics and docs. Improves stability during transient multi-tenant surges.
